title: You’ve heard of Goliath—the towering warrior, the champion of the Philistines.
paragraphs:
You’ve heard of Goliath—the towering warrior, the champion of the Philistines.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
Scripture quietly reveals that he had relatives—other giants—warriors just like him.
“These four were born to the giant in Gath, and they fell by the hand of David and by the hand of his servants.”
And in 1 Chronicles 20:4–8, we see their downfall one by one—each slain, not by David himself, but by those who stood with him.
But Here’s Where It Gets Personal…
And sometimes… you don’t just face one battle.
David defeated Goliath in 1 Samuel 17, declaring:
“The battle is the Lord’s, and He will give you into our hand.” (1 Samuel 17:47)
But the story didn’t end there.
Years later, the remaining giants appeared.
Because victory doesn’t mean the war is over.
Others finished what started with him.
And This Is Where the Gospel Breaks In
Because the real story isn’t about David.
You see, sin is the true giant.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” (Romans 3:23)
Every one of us stands on that battlefield.
And we lose—every time—on our own.
Not as a warrior with stones—but as a Savior with a cross.
“But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)
He didn’t just defeat one giant.
He crushed the root of them all.
“O death, where is your victory? O death, where is your sting?” (1 Corinthians 15:55)
Just like David’s men finished the fight…
Those who follow Christ are called to walk in His victory.
“For by grace you have been saved through faith… it is the gift of God.” (Ephesians 2:8)
There are still giants in your life.
But they don’t define the ending.
And what He started… He finishes.
Now I want to hear from you:
What “giant” are you facing right now?
